summary: One Run, one listing, and the transition the placement corpus can only assert the failure half of: a machine that does not exist becomes a machine Mercator holds. The provider negotiates a capacity lifecycle, allocates the machine in thirty-seven seconds, boots it in four minutes and seven seconds, and its node agent opens a session fifty-one seconds later. Only then is there anything to launch a workload on. What this holds at L1 that no placement fixture can is the Effect Ledger, and the ledger is the only account of what really happened to the machine: an accepted capacity.provision against the Rental Mercator minted, a node.enrolled naming that same Rental and the generation it was invited for, and the provider.launch after both. The order is the whole claim. A launch recorded before the enrolment would be Mercator creating a container through a session it does not have, and an enrolment against a Rental nothing provisioned would be a node the world invented. Nothing is terminated here, because the agent arrived: a machine that becomes executable is not a machine anybody gives back. The listing says Mercator waits eight minutes for that agent, which is deliberately neither Mercator's own fifteen nor a round number the harness holds anywhere: the same Blueprint with never_enrolls set is driven past it, and a machine handed back at eight minutes rather than at fifteen is the only evidence that the patience a provider published reached the offer at all. None of the three stage durations is a multiple of the fifteen seconds these cases reconcile at, and that is deliberate too: a control plane dating a stage from its own look would record 45, 255 and 60, and a fixture whose stages all landed on the poll grid could not tell a measured machine from a measured polling interval.
